studies.label: Laboratory team press-release experiment: unequal versus full AI access, with a common no-AI baseline
studies.cluster_se_treatment: The unadjusted AI-phase comparisons use one press-release score or one teammate-pair distance per randomized team. Table 1 uses repeated team-task submissions from both phases and does not report clustering by team or team random effects. No cluster-robust variance estimator is stated. The arm cluster counts come from the baseline team table and are not separately stated treatment-phase analysis counts. The PROCESS observation count is not reconciled with the OLS sample.

arms.name: Unequal AI access
arms.description: In the treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task, only one randomly selected member of each two-person team could use Kimi without restrictions on interaction. This is condition 1 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2). Table 3 prints the corresponding baseline team count; arm-level people counts are not printed.

arms.name: Full AI access
arms.description: Both members could use Kimi for the treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task. This is condition 2 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2). Table 3 prints the corresponding baseline team count; arm-level people counts are not printed.

arms.name: No AI access (earlier common baseline)
arms.description: Every team first wrote an electric-bicycle press release without GenAI. This is a repeated baseline phase of the same sample, not a separately randomized arm. The order and product prompt were fixed, so its comparisons with the later AI task are excluded (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2–3.3; PDF p. 14, Section 5.4).

studies.task: Two-person teams collaboratively wrote a 700-character Chinese press release about an electric bicycle without AI and then about AR glasses with their assigned AI access; each task was limited to 45 minutes (PDF p. 6, Section 3.3).

Evaluators assigned an overall grade (1–7) to the writing task submissions based on three criteria: writing quality, content quality, and originality.

estimates.notes: The eligible contrast compares the two randomized AI configurations during the treatment-phase task. Each scored press release is a team output, so the unadjusted between-team comparison has one output per randomized team; se_basis is cluster on that basis. The article does not print the test degrees of freedom or an analysis-specific observation or people count. The dispersions are explicitly labeled SD in the prose and are transcribed into the SD fields without conversion. Figure 4 on PDF p. 9 instead says its error bars are standard errors of the mean. The SD/SE discrepancy is unresolved: these values should not be treated as confirmed standardizers. The numeric fields preserve values; the source quotes preserve printed trailing zeros. No mean difference, confidence interval, or standardized effect is printed for this contrast. Quality is coded usefulness because the outcome is an overall task-quality grade including originality, rather than an explicitly named creativity rating. It is quality of a creative product press release, not an expository-writing proficiency test. Agreement audit: the outcome is scored on the jointly produced press release, so unit remains output. Its overall task-quality grade is usefulness and higher_is remains more_creative. The contrast compares randomized teams during the AI phase, so question is with_ai, outcome_with_ai is true, timing is immediate, and within_person is null (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3-3.4.2.1). The common earlier task does not make this AI-configuration contrast paired.

regression.model: OLS, Table 1 Model (1). Regresses task quality on indicators for no access and full access, with unequal access as the reference, controlling for female proportion, team problem-solving ability, team creativity, and marketing experience. These covariates were measured before treatment (PDF pp. 6 and 8). The coefficient is full minus unequal access, or control minus treatment in this record; its printed sign is retained.

estimates.notes: This is a second analysis of the same task-quality outcome and randomized AI-arm contrast, not an independent study or sample. Arm means and dispersions are in the separate unadjusted record; the regression does not print adjusted arm means. The coefficient and t statistic are copied with their negative signs: the paper models full access relative to unequal access, whereas the extraction names unequal access as treatment. No sign reversal has been calculated. The adjacent column is headed SD but contains negative entries; the footnote calls them t statistics. The adjacent value is therefore retained as the paper-labeled t statistic, with its labeling conflict flagged, and the regression SE remains null. The model N is a count of team-task submissions from the common baseline and AI phase, not a count of independent people or randomized teams. Team clustering or team random effects are not reported, so se_basis is output. No analysis-specific people counts are printed. The common no-AI baseline coefficient is excluded as nonrandomized. Agreement audit: the outcome is scored on the jointly produced press release, so unit remains output. Its overall task-quality grade is usefulness and higher_is remains more_creative. The contrast compares randomized teams during the AI phase, so question is with_ai, outcome_with_ai is true, timing is immediate, and within_person is null (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3-3.4.2.1). The common earlier task does not make this AI-configuration contrast paired.

estimates.outcome: Cognitive diversity between teammates’ spoken contributions (unadjusted comparison)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Cosine distance between the two teammates’ concatenated spoken contributions over the entire task discussion. Audio was transcribed and manually corrected; each member’s text was encoded with the Universal Sentence Encoder from TensorFlow Hub and normalized to unit length. The measure compares different people within each team, not final press releases across teams. Higher distance means greater diversity. No embedding-model version is specified (PDF p. 7, Section 3.4.3).

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.2, independent-sample comparison of unequal and full AI access
sources.quote: unequal AI access exhibited significantly higher cognitive diversity (M = 0.631, SD = 0.011) than those with full AI access (M = 0.510, SD = 0.018), t = 5.938, p < 0.01.

estimates.notes: Each team contributes one cosine distance between the pair of member-level text outputs. Thus unit is team, sd_level is pair (one pair per team), and the unadjusted independent-sample t test compares randomized team clusters. The measure is within-team, between-person diversity, not within-person flexibility and not similarity of the final written products across teams. The article prints no analysis-specific count or degrees of freedom for this t test. The arm levels and paper-labeled SDs are retained in their own units; Figure 4 on PDF p. 9 labels its error bars as standard errors of the mean, so the SD/SE conflict remains unresolved. No SE or confidence interval of the difference is printed. The model count in the PROCESS analysis is not applied to this separate t test. The mediation-model AI coefficient is excluded because that model adjusts for post-treatment interaction processes. Agreement audit: the measure compares the spoken outputs of different people, so question is across_people, construct is diversity, and higher_is is more_diverse. The two member texts yield one distance per randomized team, supporting unit team and se_basis cluster; sd_level pair describes that same non-overlapping teammate pair. It is produced during AI access, so outcome_with_ai is true, timing is immediate, and within_person is null (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3 and 3.4.3).

not_extracted.what: Cognitive diversity: AI access versus No AI access (earlier common baseline)
not_extracted.reason: The no-AI discussion occurred before AI access in every team; phase order was not randomized. It is neither an eligible randomized no-AI comparison nor an after_ai outcome (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2; PDF pp. 8–9, Section 4.2).

not_extracted.reason: These submissions were produced before either randomized AI configuration was applied. This is a baseline balance comparison, not an effect with AI or after AI removal (PDF p. 10, Section 4.4.1; PDF p. 11, Table 3).

not_extracted.reason: These discussions precede AI exposure and test initial balance rather than an eligible with-AI or after-AI effect (PDF p. 10, Section 4.4.1; PDF p. 11, Table 3).

not_extracted.reason: These paths adjust for post-treatment team interaction processes. open_items: The dispersions in Sections 4.1–4.2 (PDF pp. 8–9) are called SD, while Figure 4 says its error bars are standard errors of the mean. They are transcribed as printed SDs, but unambiguous SDs across randomized teams and confirmation of the labels are needed before standardization.

Table 1 (PDF p. 9) labels the adjacent statistic SD although it contains negative values and the footnote calls the entries t statistics. The record follows that footnote for the test field; no regression SE is supplied or reconstructed.

The paper reports 120 recruited/participating people and demographic analyses on that sample, while Table 3 reports baseline team counts of 40 and 20. It does not separately identify an analyzed people total for the creative outcomes or the baseline phase, arm-level people counts, or comparison-specific t-test counts. Study n_analyzed, baseline n_analyzed, and estimate-level people counts remain null. The randomized count retains the explicitly recruited and randomly assigned sample. Team counts are not multiplied into people counts, and model observation counts are not relabeled as people.

OLS Table 1 reports 120 team-task observations, whereas the PROCESS model reports N = 60 (PDF pp. 8–9). The paper does not reconcile these model samples or specify how repeated teams across phases enter variance estimation. The OLS record lacks reported team-clustered precision.

The external supplement remains uninspected. The main article describes writing-task instructions, evaluation instructions/examples, and interaction coding in Supplementary Sections 1-3 (PDF pp. 6-7 and 14). No matching supplement was found beside the supplied article. During reconciliation, urllib requests using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to the named Frontiers supplementary-material URL and article DOI both failed with WinError 10013. Exact scoring aggregation, originality-score details, and any additional results remain unconfirmed.
The release year of the paper-named Kimi 3.0 is not stated and remains null; the cited technical-report year does not confirm a release year for the named model.

The relationship to proceedings DOI 10.1002/pra2.1437 remains a deduplication issue: the screening form leaves overlap unconfirmed, and the citation record infers the same work but cannot confirm formal supersession. No participant-linkage statement appears in the journal PDF.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11 from both raw extractions, the supplied differences file, the screening form, the citation record, and the saved journal PDF. Read the complete markdown conversion in contiguous chunks through the final references; the saved article contains no appended appendix. Extracted every cited PDF page with pymupdf and recovered Tables 1-3 with find_tables. All retained numerical source quotes match the PDF text after whitespace normalization. The three listed study-field differences are resolved below; an additional shared_sample discrepancy in the raw files is also documented. There are no estimates only in A or only in B. Both extractors cover the same three eligible analyses; A’s slugs are retained for the unadjusted comparisons that B named ttest. No eligible estimate missing from both was found in the saved article, so n_added is 0. All counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person fields were independently checked. Screening S1-O1 is covered by the unadjusted quality and OLS estimates, with its originality variant and mediation effects listed in not_extracted. Screening S1-O2 is covered by the unadjusted diversity estimate, with its mediator-adjusted paths listed in not_extracted. Both outcomes’ earlier no-AI comparisons are excluded because phase order was fixed. Only the unequal-versus-full AI configuration comparison is randomized. The baseline remains in the arm map but is not another randomized arm or sample. Table 3 supplies team counts without converting them to people. Unknown analyzed-person counts remain null, unlike the screening form’s carried-forward experimental count. Printed statistics retain their signs and labels; no mean difference, effect size, SE, count, or value from a figure was calculated. Adjusted and unadjusted quality estimates are alternative analyses of the same outcome and sample. The unadjusted comparisons count each randomized team once; the repeated-output OLS does not report team-adjusted precision. The SD/SEM conflict and Table 1 statistic-heading conflict remain explicitly flagged. No external supplement, dataset, or proceedings full text was used. The data statement offers raw data from the authors but gives no public repository (PDF p. 14).

resolutions.decision: Retain A: null. The reported 120 is the recruited/participating experimental sample, not a separately identified analyzed people total for the creative outcomes. Demographic N values do not establish the outcome-analysis count, and Table 1 N counts submissions. No exclusions are reported, but their absence does not authorize carrying the recruitment count into this field under extraction rules 7 and 13.
